description: A curated set of 100 questions designed to assess and improve the financial knowledge and mental agility of senior citizens. Topics cover everyday money management, savings, investments, banking, taxes, and basic economic concepts.

questions.question: What is the term for the interest calculated on both the original amount and the interest already earned?
options: Simple interest
Compound interest
Fixed interest
Flat interest
questions.correct_answer: Compound interest

questions.question: If you deposit money in a savings account, the bank pays you money for keeping your funds there. What is this payment called?
options: Tax
Interest
Premium
Dividend
questions.correct_answer: Interest

questions.question: What does ATM stand for?
options: Automated Teller Machine
Automatic Transfer Mode
Annual Transaction Method
Authorized Transaction Module
questions.correct_answer: Automated Teller Machine

questions.question: Which of the following is generally considered the safest place to keep your savings?
options: Under the mattress
In a bank account
With a friend
In a piggy bank
questions.correct_answer: In a bank account

questions.question: What is a budget?
options: A type of bank loan
A plan for how to spend and save money
A government tax form
A type of investment fund
questions.correct_answer: A plan for how to spend and save money

questions.question: When prices of goods and services rise over time, this is called:
options: Deflation
Recession
Inflation
Depression
questions.correct_answer: Inflation

questions.question: What is a pension?
options: A type of home loan
Regular income paid to a person after retirement
A savings account for children
A type of insurance policy
questions.correct_answer: Regular income paid to a person after retirement

questions.question: Which document shows all the transactions in your bank account over a period of time?
options: Cheque book
Bank statement
Passbook summary
Loan agreement
questions.correct_answer: Bank statement

questions.question: What does the word 'premium' mean in an insurance policy?
options: The amount you receive when you make a claim
The regular amount you pay to keep the insurance active
The total value of assets insured
The penalty for not renewing the policy
questions.correct_answer: The regular amount you pay to keep the insurance active

questions.question: If you borrow money from a bank and must return it with extra charges, those extra charges are called:
options: Rent
Fees
Interest
Tax
questions.correct_answer: Interest

questions.question: What is a fixed deposit (FD)?
options: Money kept in a bank for a set period at a fixed rate of interest
A monthly grocery budget
A type of home loan
An account you can withdraw from at any time
questions.correct_answer: Money kept in a bank for a set period at a fixed rate of interest

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a monthly fixed expense for most people?
options: Movie tickets
Restaurant bills
Electricity bill
Birthday gifts
questions.correct_answer: Electricity bill

questions.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?
options: To earn high returns on investment
To provide financial support to family after the policyholder's death
To get discounts at hospitals
To save money on taxes only
questions.correct_answer: To provide financial support to family after the policyholder's death

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of bank account?
options: Savings account
Current account
Fixed deposit account
Trade licence account
questions.correct_answer: Trade licence account

questions.question: What does 'income' mean?
options: Money you spend on shopping
Money you earn from work, business, or investments
Money you borrow from others
Money kept in a locker
questions.correct_answer: Money you earn from work, business, or investments

questions.question: What is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?
options: The largest private bank in India
The central bank of India that manages the country's money supply
A government savings scheme for senior citizens
A foreign exchange company
questions.correct_answer: The central bank of India that manages the country's money supply

questions.question: What does the term 'nominee' mean in a bank or insurance context?
options: A person who opens the account
A person designated to receive benefits in case of the account holder's death
A person who manages your investments
A bank officer who approves your loan
questions.correct_answer: A person designated to receive benefits in case of the account holder's death

questions.question: If inflation is high, what happens to the purchasing power of your money?
options: It increases
It stays the same
It decreases
It doubles
questions.correct_answer: It decreases

questions.question: Which of the following is a government-backed small savings scheme popular among senior citizens in India?
options: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)
National Stock Exchange Fund
Mutual Fund Investment Plan
Foreign Currency Bond
questions.correct_answer: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)

questions.question: What is a mutual fund?
options: A fund where only one person invests money
A pool of money collected from many investors and invested in stocks, bonds, or other assets
A government grant for small businesses
A type of home loan product
questions.correct_answer: A pool of money collected from many investors and invested in stocks, bonds, or other assets

questions.question: What does KYC stand for in banking?
options: Know Your Capital
Keep Your Cash
Know Your Customer
Key Yearly Credentials
questions.correct_answer: Know Your Customer

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'cheque'?
options: A card used at ATMs
A written instruction to the bank to pay a specific amount to someone
A government bond certificate
A type of savings plan
questions.correct_answer: A written instruction to the bank to pay a specific amount to someone

questions.question: What is a nominee's role different from a legal heir?
options: A nominee automatically inherits all assets legally
A nominee receives assets first but may need to pass them to legal heirs as per the law
A nominee is chosen by the court
A nominee and legal heir are the same thing
questions.correct_answer: A nominee receives assets first but may need to pass them to legal heirs as per the law

questions.question: What is the main risk of keeping all your savings in cash at home?
options: The cash earns too much interest
The cash can be lost, stolen, or damaged and does not earn any interest
The bank charges fees for cash storage
The government can seize it easily
questions.correct_answer: The cash can be lost, stolen, or damaged and does not earn any interest

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a liability?
options: Money in your savings account
Your house that you own outright
A home loan you owe to the bank
Gold jewellery
questions.correct_answer: A home loan you owe to the bank

questions.question: What does GDP stand for?
options: General Deposit Plan
Gross Domestic Product
Government Development Programme
Global Distribution Policy
questions.correct_answer: Gross Domestic Product

questions.question: When the economy is in a recession, what typically happens?
options: Businesses grow and more jobs are created
Economic activity slows, businesses may close, and unemployment rises
Prices of goods fall rapidly
The government prints less money
questions.correct_answer: Economic activity slows, businesses may close, and unemployment rises

questions.question: What is a debit card?
options: A card that lets you borrow money from the bank
A card linked to your bank account that lets you spend money you already have
A card used only for online shopping
A card that earns interest every month
questions.correct_answer: A card linked to your bank account that lets you spend money you already have

questions.question: What is a credit card?
options: A card that stores your savings
A card that lets you borrow money up to a limit and pay it back later
A card used to transfer money between banks
A card issued only by the government
questions.correct_answer: A card that lets you borrow money up to a limit and pay it back later

questions.question: What happens if you do not pay your credit card bill in full by the due date?
options: The bank gives you extra credit
You are charged interest on the unpaid amount
The card gets cancelled immediately
Nothing happens for the first year
questions.correct_answer: You are charged interest on the unpaid amount

questions.question: What is the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) in India?
options: A scheme where employees and employers contribute monthly to build a retirement corpus
A government loan scheme for government employees
A monthly pension given to all citizens
A fixed deposit scheme for employees
questions.correct_answer: A scheme where employees and employers contribute monthly to build a retirement corpus

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a 'liquid' asset?
options: Real estate property
Gold ornaments locked in a bank locker
Money in a savings bank account
A fixed deposit with a 5-year lock-in
questions.correct_answer: Money in a savings bank account

questions.question: What does 'diversification' mean in investing?
options: Putting all your money in one investment for higher returns
Spreading your investments across different types to reduce risk
Investing only in foreign markets
Withdrawing money frequently
questions.correct_answer: Spreading your investments across different types to reduce risk

questions.question: Which of the following investment options is generally considered the lowest risk?
options: Stocks
Cryptocurrency
Government bonds or fixed deposits
Real estate
questions.correct_answer: Government bonds or fixed deposits

questions.question: What is a 'will' in financial and legal terms?
options: A loan document signed with the bank
A legal document that states how a person's assets should be distributed after their death
An insurance policy for the elderly
A monthly savings plan
questions.correct_answer: A legal document that states how a person's assets should be distributed after their death

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'net worth'?
options: The total amount of money you earn per year
The value of everything you own minus everything you owe
The amount of money in your bank account
The total of all your monthly expenses
questions.correct_answer: The value of everything you own minus everything you owe

questions.question: What does IFSC code stand for in Indian banking?
options: Indian Financial System Code
Internal Fund Security Code
Integrated Finance Settlement Code
International Finance Standard Code
questions.correct_answer: Indian Financial System Code

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of health insurance?
options: To invest and grow your money
To cover medical expenses in case of illness or hospitalization
To get tax refunds
To save money for retirement
questions.correct_answer: To cover medical expenses in case of illness or hospitalization

questions.question: What does the term 'maturity' mean in the context of a fixed deposit?
options: The date on which the FD reaches its end period and the money plus interest is returned
The minimum amount needed to open an FD
The interest rate offered by the bank
The penalty for early withdrawal
questions.correct_answer: The date on which the FD reaches its end period and the money plus interest is returned

questions.question: If you receive a phone call asking for your bank OTP or PIN, what should you do?
options: Share it if the caller claims to be from your bank
Share it only with family members
Never share it with anyone, as legitimate banks never ask for it
Write it down and check with the bank later
questions.correct_answer: Never share it with anyone, as legitimate banks never ask for it

questions.question: What is 'tax'?
options: A fee paid to a private company for services
A mandatory payment collected by the government from citizens and businesses
Interest earned on savings
A penalty for late loan repayment
questions.correct_answer: A mandatory payment collected by the government from citizens and businesses

questions.question: Which Indian government scheme provides guaranteed income to senior citizens above 60 years through LIC?
options: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)
Atal Pension Yojana
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
questions.correct_answer: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'expenditure'?
options: Money received as income
Money spent on goods and services
Money saved in a bank
Money borrowed from a friend
questions.correct_answer: Money spent on goods and services

questions.question: If a product is priced at Rs. 500 and there is a 10% discount, how much will you pay?
What is a 'loan EMI'?
options: The total loan amount
The interest charged per year on the loan
A fixed monthly payment made to repay a loan
The penalty for not repaying a loan
questions.correct_answer: A fixed monthly payment made to repay a loan

questions.question: What does 'nominee' mean when filling a bank account form?
options: The bank manager in charge of your account
A person who will receive your bank funds if you pass away
A co-applicant for your loan
A person who can withdraw cash on your behalf at any time
questions.correct_answer: A person who will receive your bank funds if you pass away

questions.question: What is 'supply and demand' in economics?
options: A government regulation on how much can be produced
The relationship between how much of a product is available and how much people want it, which affects prices
A method to calculate company profits
A type of bank lending system
questions.correct_answer: The relationship between how much of a product is available and how much people want it, which affects prices

questions.question: When demand for a product goes up but supply stays the same, what usually happens to the price?
options: Price decreases
Price stays the same
Price increases
Price becomes zero
questions.correct_answer: Price increases

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to protect yourself from financial fraud online?
options: Share your password with a trusted family member
Use the same password for all accounts
Use strong, unique passwords and avoid sharing personal information online
Open all links sent in emails or messages
questions.correct_answer: Use strong, unique passwords and avoid sharing personal information online

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'principal' in the context of a loan or fixed deposit?
options: The interest amount earned or charged
The original sum of money deposited or borrowed
The bank employee who manages the account
The penalty amount for early withdrawal
questions.correct_answer: The original sum of money deposited or borrowed

questions.question: What is a savings account primarily used for?
options: Storing money safely while earning some interest
Taking large loans from the bank
Buying stocks and shares
Paying direct taxes to the government
questions.correct_answer: Storing money safely while earning some interest

questions.question: What does it mean when someone says they are 'living within their means'?
options: They are spending more than they earn
They earn very little money
They spend only what they can afford based on their income
They take loans to fund daily expenses
questions.correct_answer: They spend only what they can afford based on their income

questions.question: What is 'stock' or a 'share' in a company?
options: Money deposited in a savings account
A portion of ownership in a company
A government bond
A type of insurance plan
questions.correct_answer: A portion of ownership in a company

questions.question: Why is it important to review your bank statement regularly?
options: To impress your bank manager
To check for any errors or unauthorized transactions
To calculate your income tax
It is not necessary to review it
questions.correct_answer: To check for any errors or unauthorized transactions

questions.question: What is a 'joint account' in banking?
options: An account opened in the name of a minor child
A bank account shared by two or more people
An account that earns higher interest than normal
An account opened by a company
questions.correct_answer: A bank account shared by two or more people

questions.question: What is 'tax-free income'?
options: Income on which you do not have to pay any tax to the government
Income earned only from farming
Income received as a bonus from the employer
Income from foreign countries
questions.correct_answer: Income on which you do not have to pay any tax to the government

questions.question: In India, senior citizens (above 60 years) receive a higher interest rate on:
options: Home loans
Fixed deposits in banks
Gold ETFs
Stock market investments
questions.correct_answer: Fixed deposits in banks

questions.question: What is 'UPI' used for?
options: Applying for government schemes
Transferring money digitally between bank accounts using a mobile phone
Paying insurance premiums at LIC offices
Checking your Aadhaar details
questions.correct_answer: Transferring money digitally between bank accounts using a mobile phone

questions.question: What is the National Pension System (NPS) in India?
options: A scheme that gives free food to pensioners
A voluntary long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by the government
A loan facility for retired employees
A health insurance scheme for government workers
questions.correct_answer: A voluntary long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by the government

questions.question: If you deposit Rs. 10,000 in a savings account at 4% annual interest for one year, how much interest will you earn (simple interest)?
What is the full form of NEFT in Indian banking?
options: National Electronic Funds Transfer
National Efficient Finance Transaction
New Electronic Fund Technology
National Equity Fund Transfer
questions.correct_answer: National Electronic Funds Transfer

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of a financial scam or fraud?
options: A bank sending you a monthly statement
Someone promising very high returns with zero risk
A financial advisor explaining risks before investing
Your bank updating you about new interest rates
questions.correct_answer: Someone promising very high returns with zero risk

questions.question: What is the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) scheme?
options: A scheme providing pension to senior citizens above 80 years
A pension scheme for unorganized sector workers to receive a guaranteed pension after 60
A housing loan scheme for retired government employees
A monthly allowance given to war veterans
questions.correct_answer: A pension scheme for unorganized sector workers to receive a guaranteed pension after 60

questions.question: What is meant by 'insolvency'?
options: Having more money than you need
Being unable to pay one's debts
Earning income from multiple sources
Saving a large amount every month
questions.correct_answer: Being unable to pay one's debts

questions.question: If you want to send a large amount of money (above Rs. 2 lakh) immediately to another bank account, which transfer method is best?
options: NEFT
Cheque
RTGS
Cash deposit
questions.correct_answer: RTGS

questions.question: What is a 'recurring deposit' (RD) account?
options: An account where you deposit a lump sum once and receive interest
An account where you deposit a fixed amount every month for a set period
An account where you can withdraw money any number of times
A special account for government employees only
questions.correct_answer: An account where you deposit a fixed amount every month for a set period

questions.question: What does 'interest rate' mean?
options: The number of years a loan lasts
The percentage charged on a loan or paid on a deposit
The total amount of a loan
The bank branch where you opened your account
questions.correct_answer: The percentage charged on a loan or paid on a deposit

questions.question: Why is it important to have an emergency fund?
options: To invest in the stock market
To cover unexpected expenses like medical emergencies without going into debt
To buy luxury items on sale
To avoid paying taxes
questions.correct_answer: To cover unexpected expenses like medical emergencies without going into debt

questions.question: What is a 'dividend' in the context of stocks?
options: A penalty paid to the stock exchange
A portion of a company's profits paid to shareholders
The price at which you buy a stock
The fee paid to a stockbroker
questions.correct_answer: A portion of a company's profits paid to shareholders

questions.question: Which government document in India is widely used as proof of identity and address for financial purposes?
options: Ration card
Aadhaar card
Library card
Voter ID only
questions.correct_answer: Aadhaar card

questions.question: What is 'term insurance'?
options: Insurance that covers only short-term illnesses
A pure life insurance policy that pays a sum to the family only if the insured person dies during the policy term
An insurance policy that gives monthly income for 10 years
A policy that covers only accidents
questions.correct_answer: A pure life insurance policy that pays a sum to the family only if the insured person dies during the policy term

questions.question: What happens to the value of a fixed deposit if you withdraw it before its maturity date?
options: You receive the full amount plus extra bonus
You may receive less interest or pay a penalty
The bank doubles the interest for the completed period
Nothing, you receive the same amount
questions.correct_answer: You may receive less interest or pay a penalty

questions.question: What is 'power of attorney' (POA) in financial terms?
options: A document that appoints a lawyer to fight your case in court
A legal document that authorizes another person to manage your financial affairs on your behalf
A government licence to open a business
A certificate issued by the income tax department
questions.correct_answer: A legal document that authorizes another person to manage your financial affairs on your behalf

questions.question: What is meant by the 'cost of living'?
options: The amount of money earned in a year
The total amount of money needed to cover basic expenses like food, housing, and healthcare
The interest rate on home loans
The annual bonus given by employers
questions.correct_answer: The total amount of money needed to cover basic expenses like food, housing, and healthcare

questions.question: If the inflation rate is 6% per year and your savings account gives 4% interest, what is happening to the real value of your savings?
options: It is growing
It is staying the same
It is decreasing in real terms
It is doubling
questions.correct_answer: It is decreasing in real terms

questions.question: What is 'PMJDY' – Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
options: A scheme for building houses for the poor
A financial inclusion scheme to provide bank accounts to all citizens, especially the poor
A pension scheme for senior citizens
A crop insurance scheme for farmers
questions.correct_answer: A financial inclusion scheme to provide bank accounts to all citizens, especially the poor

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'CIBIL score' or credit score in India?
options: To determine how much you can invest in stocks
To represent your creditworthiness and history of repaying loans, which banks use to decide loan approvals
To calculate your income tax
To prove your identity at the bank
questions.correct_answer: To represent your creditworthiness and history of repaying loans, which banks use to decide loan approvals

questions.question: If you pay your loan EMIs on time every month, what happens to your CIBIL credit score?
options: It decreases
It stays the same always
It generally improves over time
It is not affected by loan repayments
questions.correct_answer: It generally improves over time

questions.question: What is 'public provident fund' (PPF)?
options: A fund collected from the public for road construction
A long-term government-backed savings scheme offering tax benefits and fixed returns
A type of bank loan for buying public property
An insurance scheme by the government
questions.correct_answer: A long-term government-backed savings scheme offering tax benefits and fixed returns

questions.question: Which of the following statements about gold investment is true?
options: Gold prices never fall
Gold can act as a store of value and is considered a safe investment over the long term
Gold gives guaranteed returns every month
Gold investment is only allowed through banks
questions.correct_answer: Gold can act as a store of value and is considered a safe investment over the long term

questions.question: What is an 'annuity' in financial terms?
options: A one-time bonus payment from an employer
A series of regular payments received over a period of time, often used in retirement plans
A type of short-term loan
A penalty paid on delayed tax filing
questions.correct_answer: A series of regular payments received over a period of time, often used in retirement plans

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'collateral' in a loan?
options: The interest charged on a loan
An asset pledged as security to the lender in case the borrower cannot repay the loan
The total loan amount approved
The monthly repayment amount
questions.correct_answer: An asset pledged as security to the lender in case the borrower cannot repay the loan

questions.question: What does 'inflation-proof' investment mean?
options: An investment that earns returns higher than or equal to the inflation rate, preserving buying power
An investment that is approved by the government
An investment that cannot be withdrawn before maturity
An investment that earns no interest
questions.correct_answer: An investment that earns returns higher than or equal to the inflation rate, preserving buying power

questions.question: What is 'estate planning'?
options: Planning to buy a property or real estate
The process of deciding how your assets and wealth will be managed and distributed after your death
Filing annual income tax returns
Planning monthly household expenses
questions.correct_answer: The process of deciding how your assets and wealth will be managed and distributed after your death

questions.question: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
options: There is no difference; they work the same way
A debit card uses your own money in your account, while a credit card lets you borrow money up to a limit
A debit card is for online shopping only
A credit card earns interest on your money
questions.correct_answer: A debit card uses your own money in your account, while a credit card lets you borrow money up to a limit

questions.question: If a company's profit increases significantly, what often happens to its share price?
options: The share price usually falls
The share price usually rises
The share price stays unchanged
The company shuts down
questions.correct_answer: The share price usually rises

questions.question: What is 'money laundering'?
options: A process of cleaning coins at the bank
The illegal practice of making money obtained from crime appear to come from legal sources
A method of transferring money overseas
A way to avoid paying income tax legally
questions.correct_answer: The illegal practice of making money obtained from crime appear to come from legal sources

questions.question: What is an 'asset'?
options: Something you owe money on
Something of value that you own, such as property, gold, or money in the bank
A monthly expense
A type of government tax
questions.correct_answer: Something of value that you own, such as property, gold, or money in the bank

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of passive income?
options: Salary from a job
Selling vegetables in a market
Rent received from a property you own
Payment for driving an auto-rickshaw
questions.correct_answer: Rent received from a property you own

questions.question: What is a 'balance sheet' for a household?
options: A sheet used to balance weights in a kitchen
A summary of what a household owns (assets) and what it owes (liabilities)
A government form for filing income taxes
A record of electricity usage
questions.correct_answer: A summary of what a household owns (assets) and what it owes (liabilities)

questions.question: If a senior citizen is tricked into giving money to a stranger with a false promise of high returns, what type of crime is this?
options: Tax evasion
Financial fraud or scam
Money laundering
Insider trading
questions.correct_answer: Financial fraud or scam

questions.question: What is the benefit of a joint bank account for a senior citizen?
options: It earns double the interest
It allows a trusted family member to manage transactions if the senior citizen is unable to do so
It has no minimum balance requirement
It is only available to married couples
questions.correct_answer: It allows a trusted family member to manage transactions if the senior citizen is unable to do so

questions.question: What is 'depreciation' in simple terms?
options: An increase in the value of an asset over time
A decrease in the value of an asset over time due to use or age
A tax benefit on purchased items
A type of loan repayment
questions.correct_answer: A decrease in the value of an asset over time due to use or age

questions.question: When the government reduces the interest rate in the economy, what is one likely effect?
options: People save more money in banks
Borrowing becomes cheaper, encouraging people and businesses to take loans and spend more
Prices of goods fall immediately
The stock market always crashes
questions.correct_answer: Borrowing becomes cheaper, encouraging people and businesses to take loans and spend more

questions.question: What does 'PAN card' stand for in India and why is it important?
options: Personal Account Number – required for all banking
Permanent Account Number – a unique ID used for income tax and large financial transactions
Public Access Number – used to access government portals
Primary Authorization Number – needed for all loans
questions.correct_answer: Permanent Account Number – a unique ID used for income tax and large financial transactions

questions.question: If you take out a loan at 12% annual interest and your investment earns 8% per year, what is the wisest course of action?
options: Continue both since the investment is profitable
It is generally wiser to pay off the loan first as the interest cost exceeds investment returns
Take out a bigger loan to invest more
Close both the loan and the investment account
questions.correct_answer: It is generally wiser to pay off the loan first as the interest cost exceeds investment returns

questions.question: What is the 'rule of 72' in personal finance?
options: A rule that says you must save 72% of your income
A simple way to estimate how many years it takes to double your money by dividing 72 by the annual interest rate
A tax rule that applies after 72 years of age
A rule that says loans must be repaid in 72 months
questions.correct_answer: A simple way to estimate how many years it takes to double your money by dividing 72 by the annual interest rate

questions.question: At an interest rate of 8% per year, approximately how many years will it take to double your money using the rule of 72?
options: 6 years
9 years
12 years
18 years
questions.correct_answer: 9 years

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a government savings scheme over a private investment?
options: Government schemes always give higher returns
Government schemes are generally considered safer as they are backed by the government
Government schemes have no lock-in period
Government schemes are tax-free always
questions.correct_answer: Government schemes are generally considered safer as they are backed by the government

questions.question: Which of the following is the most responsible approach to managing money in retirement?
options: Invest all money in high-risk stocks for maximum gains
Spend all savings quickly while health is good
Balance between safe investments, regular income sources, and maintaining an emergency fund
Rely only on family members for all financial needs
questions.correct_answer: Balance between safe investments, regular income sources, and maintaining an emergency fund
